# AGENTS.md

Projen-managed **jsii** AWS CDK construct library (`@raykrueger/cdk-game-server`), TypeScript, Apache-2.0.

## Generated files — never edit directly

Projen regenerates: `package.json`, `.eslintrc.json`, `.github/`, `.projen/`, `tsconfig*.json`, `.mergify.yml`, `.gitattributes`, `.npmignore`, jest config. To change them, edit `.projenrc.js` and run `npx projen`.

`API.md` is generated by `jsii-docgen` during the build (`post-compile`). Fix doc comments in `src/` and rebuild instead of editing `API.md`.

## Commands

- `npx projen build` — full pipeline: compile (jsii) → docgen → test → package. CI runs this and fails on any self-mutation.
- **Before committing, always run `npx projen build` to completion** (it starts with a re-synth, so it also verifies generated files match `.projenrc.js`) and confirm `git status` is clean afterwards — a clean tree after build is part of the check.
- `npx projen test` — `jest --passWithNoTests --ci` then `eslint`. Snapshots are never auto-updated, so a template change fails CI instead of silently rewriting the snapshot.
- `npx projen test:update` — regenerate `test/__snapshots__` when a template change is intentional. Review the diff of the `.snap` file; it is the shape of your customers' stack.
- Single test: `npx jest test/game-server.test.ts` (or pass a `-t` test name to `npx projen test`).
- `npx projen watch` — `jsii -w` incremental compile.
- `npx projen compat` — `jsii-diff` against the published package. **Not wired into CI**; run it by hand before a breaking change. It passes `--ignore-file .compatignore`, which is not tracked in the repo.
- Compilation is `jsii`, not plain `tsc` — it enforces jsii API constraints (no enums, restricted types) on public exports.
- On Node versions jsii hasn't tested, compile prints a big warning; silence with `JSII_SILENCE_WARNING_UNTESTED_NODE_VERSION=1` if it obscures real errors.

## Upgrading projen / CDK

- `yarn upgrade projen` will NOT cross a minor boundary (caret on 0.x is minor-pinned). Use `yarn add -D projen@^X.Y.Z` instead.
- Then re-synth (`npx projen`) and verify with `npx projen build`; commit everything (source + generated) as one `chore:` commit.
- `cdkVersion` in `.projenrc.js` controls `aws-cdk-lib` (pinned devDep, `^` peer). Bump it there, not in `package.json`.
- **`cdkVersion` and `@aws-solutions-constructs/*` must move together.** Those packages carry a hard dependency on `@aws-cdk/cloud-assembly-schema`; if its major differs from the one `aws-cdk-lib` pulls in, `build » package » package:js` dies with `Conflicting versions of @aws-cdk/cloud-assembly-schema in type system`. Check the pairing before bumping: `npm view @aws-solutions-constructs/core@<ver> dependencies` and `npm view aws-cdk-lib@<ver> dependencies`. Known-good pair: cdk `2.278.0` + solutions-constructs `^2.107.0` (both on schema v55).
- Those two deps are declared with explicit versions in `.projenrc.js`, so projen treats them as pinned and leaves them out of the daily `upgrade` task's `--filter=` list (see `.projen/tasks.json`). Bump them by hand with `cdkVersion` — that is intentional, since upgrading them independently is what reintroduces the schema conflict.
- `npx projen upgrade` bumps *all* deps and is what the `upgrade-main` workflow runs daily.
- Projen records its own version in `package.json` `devDependencies` at synth time, so the `yarn add` + `npx projen` pair is what actually lands the version bump.
- A projen minor bump usually rewrites CI workflows. As of 0.105 the self-mutation job is its own `.github/workflows/self-mutation.yml` (triggered by `workflow_run` on `build`) instead of a job inside `build.yml`. Still needs the `PROJEN_GITHUB_TOKEN` secret.

## Toolchain versions and their ceilings

Several dev-tool majors are deliberately held back. Check this before "just upgrading" them.

| Package | Pinned to | Why it cannot go higher right now |
|---|---|---|
| Node (`minNodeVersion`) | 24 | Sets `engines.node >= 24`, every CI `setup-node`, and `@types/node` |
| TypeScript | 6.x | `jsii@6` pins `typescript ~6.0`, `jsii@5.9` pins `~5.9`, and `ts-jest` peers `>=4.3 <7`. TS 7 is out until both move |
| ESLint | 9.x | projen's `Eslint` component only emits `.eslintrc.json` and runs it with `ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false`. ESLint 10 dropped eslintrc: it refuses `.eslintrc.json` and legacy flags, so the `eslint` task breaks. Needs projen flat-config support first |
| `@stylistic/eslint-plugin` | ^2 | Hardcoded in projen's `Eslint` component (`eslint.js`, only skipped when `eslintOptions.prettier` is on). Requesting `^6` throws a dependency version conflict at synth |

- `jsiiVersion` in `.projenrc.js` moves **jsii and jsii-rosetta together** (`projen/lib/cdk/jsii-build.js` adds both with the same suffix). Bump `typescriptVersion` in the same commit.
- The jest knob is `jestOptions: { jestVersion: '^30' }` — `jestVersion` is a `JestOptions` field. At the top level projen **silently ignores** it. Projen then pins `@types/jest` to the same range and picks `ts-jest@^29` for jest >= 30.
- To force a version for a dependency that a projen component also declares, call `project.addDevDeps('name@^X')` **after** construction, next to the LICENSE patch. Components run during construction and `Dependencies.addDependency()` overwrites, so a range in the `devDeps` option gets wiped by the component's versionless `addDevDeps()` call. Seen with `eslint-import-resolver-typescript@^4`.

## Releases / npm publishing

Releases are fully automatic on push to `main` — nothing is published by hand.

- **Only `feat:` and `fix:` commits ship.** `.projenrc.js` sets `releasableCommits: ReleasableCommits.featuresAndFixes()` (projen's own default is `everyCommit()`, which published on every push). A push of `chore:`/`docs:`/`ci:` commits still runs `release.yml`, but `bump` reports "No new interesting commits", `dist/releasetag.txt` stays at the current tag, `tag_exists` comes back true, and both publish jobs are skipped. So a chore-only push is release-neutral.
- Caveat: the type comes from a POSIX-ERE grep on the commit **subject** (`^(feat|fix)(\(scope\))?!?: `), and Mergify squash-merges with the PR title as the subject — so the PR title must be a valid conventional commit or the change never releases.
- Version comes from conventional commits via `commit-and-tag-version@^13` (`npx projen release` → `bump`). `package.json` in git always says `0.0.0`; `release` bumps, builds, then `unbump` resets it. Never hand-edit `version`.
- `majorVersion` is projen's default (`ONE`): the first component stays 0 and a breaking change bumps the **minor** slot — that is how `fix!: rename hostzedZone to hostedZone` went `0.0.47 → 0.1.0`.
- Artifacts (`dist/releasetag.txt`, `dist/version.txt`, `dist/changelog.md`, `dist/js/*.tgz`) are build output only. **`CHANGELOG.md` is not tracked in git** — the generated changelog becomes the GitHub Release body.
- Merge path is Mergify: squash-merge queue requiring 1 approval plus `build` and `package-js` status checks (`.mergify.yml`).
- Publishing to npm uses **npm trusted publishing** (GitHub Actions OIDC, `npmTrustedPublishing: true` in `.projenrc.js`) — there is no `NPM_TOKEN` secret. The trusted publisher is configured on the npm side (package → "Trusted publishers" → this repo / `release.yml`); if publishing suddenly 403s, check that config first. `publib-npm` also runs with `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE=true`.
- npm is phasing out direct publish with bypass-2FA tokens (targeting Jan 2027); keep using trusted publishing rather than reintroducing a token.
- `release.yml` supports a manual `[DRY RUN]` (`workflow_dispatch` → `dry_run`) which sets `PUBLIB_DRYRUN` and skips `gh release create`. Useful to test release changes without publishing.
- Only the **js** target is built (`jsii.targets: {}`) — no PyPI/Maven bindings.

## Layout

- `src/index.ts` — the `GameServer` construct (VPC, EFS, Fargate task/service, spot capacity). Entry point via `src/index.ts` exports.
- `src/auto_shutdown.ts`, `src/discord.ts`, `src/discord-state-machine.ts`, `src/discord_bot_custom_resource.ts` — optional feature constructs wired up by `GameServer`.
- `resources/functions/` — inline **Python** Lambda sources, bundled via `Code.fromAsset` at synth time (do not add non-Lambda build tooling expectations here).
- `test/game-server.test.ts` — the only test file: 12 template (`Template.fromStack`) tests plus one full-stack snapshot, ~99% statement coverage of `src/`. It synthesizes with `context: { 'aws:cdk:bundling-stacks': [] }`, which makes CDK skip Lambda asset bundling; without it the suite needs the Docker socket that GitHub Actions runners deny. Keep that context on any new `App` you add here.
- The snapshot is committed. Because the test task runs `--ci` (projen `updateSnapshot: NEVER`), an unintended CloudFormation change fails the build; run `npx projen test:update` only when the change is meant.

## Conventions

- Git: conventional commits, signed (`git commit -s`), no co-authored-by/Generated-by trailers.
- Version is 0.x with no backwards-compatibility guarantees. `jsii-diff` compat is **not** run by CI — check it manually with `npx projen compat`.
- Commit messages drive the release, so conventional-commit prefixes matter, and only `feat:`/`fix:` (optionally with `!` for breaking) are releasable at all. `fix!:` = minor bump, `feat:`/`fix:` = patch/minor; `chore:`/`docs:`/`ci:` never publish — if a dependency or peer-range change must reach consumers, label it `fix:`.
